title: Saraburi–Nakhon Nayok 2D1N Trip — Waterfalls & Khao Yai Foothills | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Two-province road trip: Saraburi's Chet Sao Noi Falls and Muak Lek dairy farms, then cross into Nakhon Nayok for Sarika Falls, Nang Rong, Wang Takrai, and Khun Dan Dam — with timed itinerary, entry fees, and real food stops.
keywords: Saraburi Nakhon Nayok trip, Chet Sao Noi waterfall, Sarika waterfall, Nang Rong waterfall, Wang Takrai, Khao Yai foothills itinerary
intro: Saraburi and Nakhon Nayok sit on opposite flanks of the Khao Yai massif — both packed with cool waterfalls, green meadows, and mountain-fresh air less than two hours from Bangkok. This trip splits over two days and one night: Day 1 tackles the Muak Lek side of Saraburi, Day 2 crosses into Nakhon Nayok for a completely different style of waterfall — all in a single loop.

blocks.html: The charm of this trip is comparing waterfalls on both sides of the same mountain range in one go. Muak Lek on the Saraburi side is all about shallow, wade-friendly cascades and dairy farms; Nakhon Nayok on the other side is dramatic cliff-face waterfalls pouring down from the southern edge of Khao Yai. The main route runs along Mittraphap Highway and the bypass roads — easiest by car. No car? You can rent one in Saraburi town or book a private minivan for half a day.

blocks.title: Before you go
blocks.html: Both provinces' waterfalls peak between late rainy season and early cool season — roughly October to January. During the dry months (March–April) water levels drop significantly. If swimming is the goal, check the national park's official water-level updates first. Pack water-shoes and a change of clothes.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Saraburi Side: Muak Lek & the Dairy Farm

blocks.html: Day 1 heads out from Bangkok along Mittraphap Highway into Muak Lek district — about 130 km, roughly 1.5–2 hours. This side packs in a waterfall, a working dairy farm, and a hillside café all in one day.

items.activity: Leave Bangkok — head north on Mittraphap Highway toward Muak Lek
items.note: Grab coffee at any roadside petrol station along the way. Morning traffic is light on this stretch.

items.activity: Chet Sao Noi Waterfall — walk the lower tiers and wade in
items.note: Open 08:00–16:30. Entry: adults 20 THB, children 10 THB. The lower tiers are shallow and rocky — waterproof sandals or water-shoes are a must.

items.activity: Drive to Thai–Denmark Dairy Farm (DPO Muak Lek) — farm ride, calf feeding, cowboy show
items.note: Thailand's original dairy cooperative. Visitor activities include a tractor tour of the farm, bottle-feeding calves, and a Thai cowboy show.

items.activity: Lunch in Muak Lek — local beef steak or a meadow-view restaurant
items.note: Souvenirs to grab here: fresh milk, yogurt, and caramel milk candy straight from the farm.

items.activity: Optional: hillside café in Muak Lek or Pa Sak Jolasid Dam (Wang Muang side)
items.note: Pick one based on time. The dam has wide open views — great for photos in the late afternoon light.

items.activity: Check into accommodation near Muak Lek or back in Saraburi town
items.note: The Muak Lek–Pak Chong stretch has mountain-view resorts at various price points.

blocks.title: Pick the right base for Day 2
blocks.html: If you're crossing into Nakhon Nayok the next morning, staying in southern Saraburi or Muak Lek cuts out a lot of early-morning driving — the route south skips Saraburi town entirely.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Saraburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 2 — Cross into Nakhon Nayok: Cliff Waterfalls & Natural Water Parks

blocks.html: Morning of Day 2, drive south from the Saraburi side into Nakhon Nayok — about 70–90 km from Muak Lek depending on the route, roughly 1.5 hours. The waterfalls here are a completely different character from Chet Sao Noi: sheer cliff drops fed by the southern face of Khao Yai.

items.activity: Leave accommodation — head to Hin Tang sub-district, Nakhon Nayok
items.note: The road hugs the foothills — you'll pass orchards and open fields most of the way.

items.activity: Nang Rong Waterfall — walk the trail and soak in the lower pool
items.note: Inside Khao Yai National Park. Medium-sized, easy trail, family-friendly swimming. Entry: adults 40 THB, children 20 THB (national park rate).

items.activity: Wang Takrai Park — lunch beside the stream in the shade
items.note: Open 08:00–17:00. Vehicle entry 150 THB per car (up to 8 people); walk-in 20 THB. Shaded trails and a creek running through — a good rest stop between waterfalls.

items.activity: Sarika Waterfall — take in the cliff-face cascade
items.note: Multi-tiered falls dropping nearly 200 m off a sheer cliff face. Open 08:00–17:00. Entry: adults 40 THB, children 20 THB. Nakhon Nayok's most iconic waterfall.

items.activity: Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam — reservoir and mountain views
items.note: One of Thailand's longest roller-compacted concrete dams. Wide lake and mountain panorama — works best for photos in the mid-to-late afternoon.

items.activity: Pick up marian plums and local snacks before heading back to Bangkok
items.note: Nakhon Nayok is famous for marian plums (maying chit) and sweet maprang. Peak season is February–March; outside season you'll find processed versions.

items: Bangkok → Muak Lek — approx. 130 km via Mittraphap Highway, 1.5–2 hrs drive
Muak Lek → Nakhon Nayok town — approx. 70–90 km along the foothills, 1.5 hrs drive
Nakhon Nayok → Bangkok — approx. 110–120 km via Ongkharak, 1.5–2 hrs drive

No car? You can still do it: take a train to Kaeng Khoi then a local songthaew into Muak Lek. For Nakhon Nayok, minivans run from Victory Monument — then charter a songthaew for the waterfall circuit by the day.

blocks.title: Honest heads-up
blocks.html: Two provinces in two days is a fairly packed schedule. Travelling with young kids or older relatives? Trim the list — on Day 2 one or two Nakhon Nayok waterfalls plus Wang Takrai is plenty for a relaxed pace without rushing between stops.

blocks.text: What to Eat Along the Way

blocks.html: The food scene is pretty different on each side. Saraburi's Muak Lek is all about fresh dairy and local beef. Nakhon Nayok leans toward open-air riverside restaurants, cha muang leaf curry, and boat noodles.

items.name: Muak Lek dairy eats
items.blurb: Fresh milk, yogurt, and caramel milk toffee straight from the cooperative farm — plus affordable local beef steak joints nearby.

items.name: Nakhon Nayok open-air restaurants
items.blurb: Paddy-field eateries with wide views and breezy seating. Red tilapia and river prawns are house staples at most spots.

items.name: Nakhon Nayok boat noodles
items.blurb: Small-bowl boat noodles with rich, dark broth — eat them perched over the water. One of the province's most-loved street snacks.

items: Late rainy to early cool season (Oct–Jan) — waterfalls running full, cool mountain air, the most photogenic conditions
February–March — marian plum season in Nakhon Nayok; you can buy fruit fresh from the orchard
March–May — dry season, waterfalls shrink; better for scenic views than swimming
Avoid visiting waterfalls immediately after heavy rain — flash floods can hit fast and rocks get dangerously slippery. Check national park announcements before you go.

faq.q: Can you visit both Saraburi and Nakhon Nayok on one trip?
faq.a: Absolutely. The two provinces sit on opposite sides of the Khao Yai range, only about 70–90 km apart. A 2D1N trip works perfectly — Day 1 on the Muak Lek/Saraburi side, Day 2 across in Nakhon Nayok.

faq.q: How are the waterfalls in Saraburi different from Nakhon Nayok's?
faq.a: Saraburi's falls — like Chet Sao Noi and those around Muak Lek — are low, tiered cascades that are easy to wade in, great for families with kids. Nakhon Nayok's Sarika and Nang Rong are tall cliff-face drops fed by the southern wall of Khao Yai: more dramatic to look at, but the rocks are slippery so more care is needed.

faq.q: How much is the entry fee at each waterfall?
faq.a: Chet Sao Noi: adults 20 THB, children 10 THB. Sarika and Nang Rong (Khao Yai National Park rate): adults 40 THB, children 20 THB. Wang Takrai: vehicle entry 150 THB per car (up to 8 people) or walk-in 20 THB per person. Prices may change — double-check at the gate.

faq.q: Is it possible to do this trip without a car?
faq.a: Yes, but it takes more planning. For Saraburi, take a train to Kaeng Khoi then a local songthaew to Muak Lek. For Nakhon Nayok, minivans run from Victory Monument in Bangkok, then charter a songthaew for the waterfall loop. If flexibility matters, renting a car is still the most convenient option.

faq.q: When are the waterfalls at their best?
faq.a: Late rainy season into early cool season — roughly October through January. Water levels are high and the air in the foothills is cool and fresh. During the dry months (March–April) water levels drop a lot; fine for scenery but not really for swimming.
